items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I’m thinking of Sinatra with Night and Day or something like that, The Cole Porter Story.

ctx.x: He called up Jack and reamed him out.

Here’s this famous article that he wrote – he wrote an op-ed in the [New York] Times – that I – this is when I do my reharmonized standards class. I say there’s two sides to the story here. There’s play it like it is, or like it was, or play it the way you hear it. I say, “Alec Wilder” – first of all, I explain who he was – “I want to read you this article,” because Vic gave me this article. It was from the ’50s, how he said, “Would you change ‘To be or not to be’?” He said, “What gives a jazz musician the right…
But he was definitely an interesting man. About a week after I saw him, I got a postcard in the mail from him, thanking me for coming and blah blah blah.
